Analyzing voltius-git AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe for the narrow gate of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

**Top-level scope analysis:** The PKGBUILD's global scope contains only variable assignments and a `source` array with two entries: a `git+https://github.com/VoltiusApp/voltius.git` source (the project's own upstream repository) and a `$_pkgname.desktop` file. Both have `SKIP` checksums, which is standard practice for VCS sources and harmless text assets. There are no command substitutions, `eval` calls, or dangerous commands at the top level.

**`pkgver()` analysis:** The `pkgver()` function runs `git describe --long --tags | sed 's/^v//;s/\([^-]*-g\)/r\1/;s/-/./g'` after `cd` into the cloned source. This is a completely standard pattern used in countless `-git` packages to derive the version from git tags, and it executes no untrusted code.

**Out of scope for this gate:** The `prepare()` (npm install of pnpm), `build()` (pnpm install, tauri build), and `package()` (install of built binary and assets) functions will not execute during `--nobuild --noprepare`, so they are not relevant to this safety decision and will be reviewed separately.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard -git PKGBUILD; sourcing and source fetching are safe.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices for a -git VCS package. The source is cloned from the project's own upstream repository at `https://github.com/VoltiusApp/voltius.git`, which is the expected behavior for a -git package. Both checksums are set to `SKIP`, which is required for VCS sources and is a normal hygiene choice, not a malicious indicator.

The `prepare()` step installs `pnpm` locally via `npm install -g pnpm@10.34.5 --prefix "$srcdir/npm-global"` to work around pnpm not being in the official Arch repositories. This downloads from the official npm registry with a pinned version, which is a reasonable and common pattern for AUR packages needing npm-based tooling.

The `build()` step is standard for a Tauri/Rust application: it sets the linker, uses the locally installed pnpm, sets dummy Tauri signing keys (explicitly labeled as such for AUR builds), and runs `pnpm tauri build --no-bundle`. The `package()` step performs routine installation of the binary, license, desktop file, and icons into the appropriate system paths.

No suspicious network requests to unexpected hosts, no obfuscated code, no exfiltration attempts, no backdoors, and no use of dangerous commands like `eval` or `base64` decoding are present.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard AUR packaging for a Tauri/Rust git package; no malicious behavior detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>
